extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting speculative short fiction to Strange Horizons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting short speculative-fiction stories to the online magazine Strange Horizons, including content, length, rights, formatting, and submission procedures. Intended to help authors determine eligibility and the correct submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre: speculative fiction (broadly defined)
rubrics_metrics.description: We want: Speculative fiction, broadly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your story doesn’t have a speculative element, or strong speculative-fiction sensibilities, it’s probably not for us. We welcome all subgenres and forms of speculative fiction (see exclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions: horror, the grotesque, and erotica
rubrics_metrics.description: We are also not a horror market. We welcome all subgenres and forms of speculative fiction, excepting horror/the grotesque and erotica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please don’t query to ask if we’re interested in a particular subgenre; you can assume that even if it’s not listed above, it’s okay — except for the exclusions listed here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred and allowed lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 10,000 words (under 5000 preferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We prefer stories under 5,000 words, but we consider stories up to 10,000 words. Note, however, that the longer the story is, the less likely we are to be interested. Our wordcount limit is not absolutely inflexible, but we can’t consider stories much over the limit, not even as serials. We have no minimum wordcount requirement and will consider short-short stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordcount measurement rule
rubrics_metrics.description: We determine story length by taking the word-processor wordcount and rounding up to the next highest 100 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your word processor's count; the magazine will round up to the next 100 for their consideration and payment calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable lengths/forms: novellas, serialized novels, very long stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories much above 10,000 words, including serialized novels or novellas, will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The limit is firm in practice — stories considerably over 10,000 words are not suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously unpublished in English requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously unpublished in English—we buy first English publication rights, including audio rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will consider stories which have previously appeared in another language, but have never been published in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights purchased and exclusivity period
rubrics_metrics.description: We buy first-printing world exclusive English-language rights (including audio rights) for six (6) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After that period you are free to republish the story elsewhere. We hope you’ll allow us to leave the story in our archives indefinitely after it’s rotated off the main table of contents, but you have the right to remove your story from the archives at any time after one (1) year.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unsolicited reprints previously published in English
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsolicited reprints of works previously published in English will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the work has been published in English before, do not submit it as new material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method: gateway/online form only
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted through our submission gateway—no email or postal submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In order to track stories correctly, we can only consider stories submitted through that form—no email or paper mail submissions. Upload a file in Rich Text Format (RTF) using the submission form.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a file in Rich Text Format using our submission form. Don’t worry about font, font size, line spacing or indentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Our system automatically reformats submissions the way we like them, so authors need not worry about specific formatting details.

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous or multiple submissions / no multiple stories
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous or multiple submissions; no re-submissions; multiple stories at once from the same author are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions sent to us and another venue simultaneously are not allowed. Stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons, even if they have been revised, are not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: No partial or incomplete stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial or incomplete stories are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please don’t send us part of a story and ask us to request the rest of it if we’re interested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t need to see a cover letter, but if you provide one, keep it short and list a few of your most recent or most relevant publications or workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have life experience relevant to your story (e.g. your story takes place on a submarine, and you served on a submarine), please mention that. Cover letters shouldn’t include plot synopses or pitches. The site links to sample cover letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rate and minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay 8¢/word (USD), with a minimum payment of $60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rates are stated in USD; payment calculation follows the magazine's rounded wordcount rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment timing and method
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of 8¢/word USD, within 60 days of contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SFWA officially considers Strange Horizons a professional market. They pay by check or PayPal, according to the author’s preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and querying policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We usually respond within three weeks, but always respond in less than 40 days. After 40 days, if you haven’t heard from us, please query immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven’t heard within 40 days, query. The response status page shows exactly how long they’ve been considering stories; if you’ve submitted before that date, query immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autoresponder expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: We send an autoresponder message in response to every submission we receive. If you haven’t received an autoresponse within 24 hours after submitting, please query immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing an autoresponse usually means they have an incorrect email address for you, and won’t be able to contact you when they make a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit a story, we strongly prefer you don’t withdraw it. If you withdraw a story, we won’t consider any version of that story in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do need to withdraw a story, please send an e-mail telling them you need to withdraw the story and let them know why. The policy is strict: withdrawn stories are barred from future consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content standards: profanity, sex, violence, gore
rubrics_metrics.description: Profanity is fine. Sex or violence in a story should be artistically justified; no excessive gore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use whatever words are appropriate for your story, but avoid gratuitous gore; sexual content should have artistic justification rather than be pornographic (see erotica exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and representation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction from or about diverse perspectives and traditionally under-represented groups, settings, and cultures, written from a non-exoticizing and well-researched position, is especially welcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editors are interested in work that treats diverse perspectives respectfully and with research; avoid exoticizing portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and structure openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual yet readable styles and inventive structures and narratives are welcomed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine is open to experimental approaches provided the work remains readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political and thematic complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that address political issues in complex and nuanced ways, resisting oversimplification, are of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They prefer nuanced examinations of political themes rather than simplistic or didactic treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypertext fiction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypertext fiction is of interest; if you have a work of hyperfiction you think might be a good fit, please query to discuss how to submit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyperfiction may require special submission/technical handling; contact the editors before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and spelling acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome submissions from anywhere in the world, and British spellings are fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine accepts international submissions and variants of English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously submitted to Strange Horizons prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons, even if they have been revised, will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not resubmit a story that has ever been sent to Strange Horizons before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response-status transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a response status page that is automatically updated and shows exactly how long they’ve been considering stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are waiting for a response about a story you sent before the date listed on the response-status page, you should query immediately.
